column14: No per-sample type table exists for the 1000 Genomes LCLs, so the test is a population prediction over 26 populations with a large n: type 2 should be concentrated in the African-ancestry panels and rare elsewhere, and its reading should be proportional to the chrEBV load the cohort already publishes. The background includes the reference's own chrEBV (NC_007605.1, type 1) and five further type-1 genomes (Akata KC207813.1, Mutu KC207814.1, M81 KF373730.1, GD1 AY961628.3, Raji KF717093.1), so only type-2-diagnostic k-mers survive: 1,623 of the 10,690 candidates were dropped as type-1 background.
column19: EBV type 2 is not in GRCh38 in any form; chrEBV is type 1. Unlike the other six classes, most EBV-2 reads will still align - to chrEBV, at type-1/type-2 identity of about 80-96% in these genes - so the class's reads are split between chrEBV and the unmapped bin in a proportion no one has measured. That split is exactly what scans have to establish before any fetch: the honest fetch plan is chrEBV plus the unmapped bin, and the sinks must be learned like everyone else's.
column20: 0 reads in the five unmapped bins tested here, which is expected both because type 2 is uncommon in these lines and because most EBV reads align to chrEBV rather than falling in the unmapped bin - this class cannot be read from the unmapped bin alone. The k-mers come from one type-2 strain, so a divergent type-2 virus reads low (Jijoye still gives 0.95). A nonzero reading needs a floor set for index hopping and cross-sample contamination, which the PHIX class measures, and it has a second floor from type 1 itself that scales with EBV load: type-1 reads with a sequencing error or a minor variant at a site where the types differ by one base carry 4-31 EBV2 k-mers. In NA12878 (an LCL transformed with B95-8, type 1) 34 of its 1,777,780 chrEBV records (27 not duplicate-flagged), 1.9e-5, carry >= 4 EBV2 k-mers, all at chrEBV 79,941-87,429 (the EBNA-3 block) and none in the EBNA-2 block, where the types differ most (the test fixture's 4,621 chrEBV reads give 0, as expected). chrEBV records in the 1,748 counted scans range from 126,194 to 30,872,944 (median 1,089,570), so at that rate the floor is about 21 reads in the median genome, 96 at the 95th percentile and up to about 590. Because it is proportional to the chrEBV load, as a true type-2 reading also is, type 2 has to be called from the EBV2/chrEBV read ratio well above 2e-5, or from reads in the EBNA-2 block, not from a count threshold. The complementary measurement - the B95-8 deletion window chrEBV:144,445-151,554, which detects donor wild-type virus - is a reference region for controls.bed, not a panel class, and is not built here.
